scenarios.title: User cannot log in after password reset
scenarios.summary: Practice triage for a login failure that surfaces after a password reset, separating account state from client/browser noise.
scenarios.report: "I reset my password from the email link. New password is accepted on the reset page, but when I try to sign in with demo.user@example.com I still get Invalid credentials. Cleared cookies twice."
scenarios.objective: Reproduce the login path, confirm account and reset-token state, and decide whether this is user error, stale session, or account lockout before escalating.
scenarios.impact: One demo counselor cannot access the practice portal; no other roles reported.
scenarios.note: Simulation for practice — fictional demo account and reset ticket. Not a production incident claim.

triage.question: When did the last successful login occur?
triage.answer: Yesterday 16:40 IST, before the reset email was requested.

triage.question: Was the reset link opened once or multiple times?
triage.answer: Opened twice; first attempt timed out, second completed with green success banner.

triage.question: Exact error text on sign-in?
triage.answer: Invalid credentials — generic message, no lockout countdown shown.

triage.question: Same failure in a private window?
triage.answer: Not yet tried by the reporter.

hypotheses.label: Stale session / old cookies conflicting with new password
Wrong email or typo on the sign-in form
Reset completed in UI but password not persisted
Account temporarily locked after failed attempts

actions.label: Reproduce sign-in with the reported email in a fresh private window
actions.feedback: Useful test — establishes a clean baseline without cached session noise.
actions.result: Private window also returns Invalid credentials for demo.user@example.com with the password from the reset confirmation email.
actions.evidence: Reproduced Invalid credentials in private Chrome; not solely a local cookie issue.

actions.label: Confirm email spelling against the password-reset confirmation screen
actions.feedback: Useful test — rules out simple identity mismatch early.
actions.result: Reset confirmation shows demo.user@example.com. Sign-in form matches. No typo found.
actions.evidence: Email identity consistent across reset confirmation and sign-in form.

actions.label: Inspect POST /api/demo/auth/login in DevTools Network
actions.feedback: Useful test — status and payload separate client messaging from server decision.
actions.result: POST returns 401 with body {"error":"invalid_credentials","attemptsRemaining":3}. No Set-Cookie session issued.
actions.evidence: Login API returns 401 invalid_credentials; account not yet locked (3 attempts remaining).

actions.label: Review demo password-reset audit for PWD-RESET-4412
actions.feedback: Useful test — confirms whether the new hash was written.
actions.result: Audit shows reset_token_consumed=true but password_hash_updated=false with note token_replay_ignored. First timed-out submit may have raced; second UI success did not persist.
actions.evidence: Reset ticket shows token consumed without password hash update — reset incomplete server-side.

actions.label: Ask user to clear browser cache again and retry
actions.feedback: Low-information — already reproduced in a private window.
actions.result: Same Invalid credentials after another cache clear. No new signal.
actions.evidence: Additional cache clear did not change outcome.

actions.label: Issue a fresh password-reset link and validate hash update before next login attempt
actions.feedback: Useful next step once incomplete reset is evidenced.
actions.result: New reset PWD-RESET-4419 completes with hash_updated=true. Subsequent login succeeds and sets session cookie.
actions.evidence: Fresh reset with confirmed hash update restores login — original reset was incomplete, not a permanent account issue.

actions.label: Restart the user's computer and retry login
actions.feedback: Premature — no OS-layer signal; wastes time before account-state checks.
actions.result: Restart completes; login still fails until a proper reset is issued. No diagnostic value.
actions.evidence: OS restart did not change authentication outcome.

completion.fixMessage: Incomplete password reset (token consumed without hash update). Fresh reset with verified hash_updated=true restores access.

scenarios.title: Counselor gets 403 updating assigned lead
scenarios.summary: Isolate a role-aware lead update failure: same lead works for admin, fails for counselor — authorization vs client vs network.
scenarios.report: "I open Lead #1842 (assigned to me) and click Save after changing status to Contacted. The UI says You don't have permission. Admin says the lead looks fine. Edge and Chrome both fail for me."
scenarios.objective: Prove whether the 403 is role/permission, record ownership, client bug, or environment — then package evidence for escalation if needed.
scenarios.impact: Counselors cannot progress assigned leads; admins unaffected. Demo pipeline stalled for Lead #1842.
scenarios.note: Simulation inspired by role-aware workflow thinking explored in Catalyx — not a production incident claim.

triage.question: Is Lead #1842 assigned to the reporter?
triage.answer: Assignment panel shows counselor.demo@example.com as owner.

triage.question: Does read (GET) succeed while update fails?
triage.answer: Lead detail page loads; only Save / status change fails.

triage.question: Any recent permission or role change?
triage.answer: Demo role matrix updated two days ago for lead.write scope.

triage.question: Admin result on the same lead?
triage.answer: Not yet compared by the reporter — flagged for isolation.

triage.question: Exact UI message?
triage.answer: You don't have permission to update this lead.

hypotheses.label: Counselor role missing lead.write / update permission
Ownership check failing despite assignment UI
Browser-specific client bug
Network or proxy stripping auth headers
Stale cached permission decision

actions.label: Reproduce as counselor: open Lead #1842 and PATCH status to Contacted
actions.feedback: Useful test — confirms the failure path under the reported role.
actions.result: Save fails. UI toast: You don't have permission. Network shows PATCH 403.
actions.evidence: Counselor PATCH Lead #1842 → 403 forbidden, reason role_lacks_permission.

actions.label: Test admin on the same Lead #1842 status update
actions.feedback: Useful test — isolates role/permission from record corruption.
actions.result: Admin saves successfully. Status becomes Contacted. PATCH returns 200.
actions.evidence: Admin update succeeds on Lead #1842 — record is writable; failure is role-scoped.

actions.label: Retry as counselor in Edge (clean profile)
actions.feedback: Useful test — checks browser-specific client bugs.
actions.result: Same 403 and same toast in Edge. Not browser-specific.
actions.evidence: Counselor 403 reproduces in Edge — not a Chrome-only client bug.

actions.label: Inspect HTTP PATCH and GET payloads for Lead #1842
actions.feedback: Useful test — status code and reason field pinpoint authorization.
actions.result: GET /api/demo/leads/1842 returns 200 with assignee counselor.demo@example.com. PATCH returns 403 with role_lacks_permission / lead.write. Authorization header present on both.
actions.evidence: Read allowed, write denied with explicit missing lead.write on counselor role.

actions.label: Clear browser cache and hard-reload the lead page
actions.feedback: Low-information — 403 is server-authored with a stable reason code.
actions.result: Hard reload still yields PATCH 403. No change.
actions.evidence: Cache clear did not alter 403 response.

actions.label: Restart the computer and retry
actions.feedback: Low-information / premature for an authorization 403.
actions.result: After restart, counselor still receives 403 on PATCH. No new evidence.
actions.evidence: OS restart irrelevant to role_lacks_permission response.

actions.label: Check Wi-Fi / general network connectivity
actions.feedback: Low-information for this scenario — GET succeeds and admin path works.
actions.result: Connectivity fine. Other API calls succeed. Issue remains role-scoped 403.
actions.evidence: Network healthy; failure is authorization, not connectivity.

actions.label: Prepare escalation note with role matrix gap and HTTP evidence
actions.feedback: Useful once enough evidence exists — structured handover over vague access issue.
actions.result: Escalation draft ready: counselor lacks lead.write; GET OK / PATCH 403; admin OK on Lead #1842; reproduces Chrome+Edge; request IDs from demo Network tab attached.
actions.snippet:
Summary: Counselor role missing lead.write
Record: Lead #1842
Evidence: PATCH 403 role_lacks_permission; Admin PATCH 200
Ask: Confirm role matrix for counselor lead updates
actions.evidence: Escalation package prepared with expected/actual, roles compared, and HTTP snippets.

completion.fixMessage: Counselor role lacks lead.write. Lead #1842 is valid; admin succeeds. Fix is permission matrix / RBAC config — not client or network.

scenarios.title: Intermittent API timeout vs 500 on demo endpoint
scenarios.summary: Practice reading status codes as clues: intermittent timeout and occasional 500 on the same demo endpoint are not the same root cause story.
scenarios.report: "Calling GET /api/demo/reports/summary sometimes spins for 30s then fails, sometimes returns 500. Postman and the app both do it. Happens maybe 1 in 4 requests."
scenarios.objective: Separate client timeout, gateway timeout, and application 500; capture enough correlation IDs to escalate without guessing.
scenarios.impact: Demo dashboard summary widget unreliable; other CRUD APIs appear stable.
scenarios.note: Fictional demo API path and correlation IDs only — not a claim about a live production service.

triage.question: Exact path and method?
triage.answer: GET /api/demo/reports/summary?range=7d

triage.question: Always the same status?
triage.answer: No — mix of client abort ~30s and HTTP 500 with JSON error body.

triage.question: Other endpoints affected?
triage.answer: GET /api/demo/leads?limit=10 stays ~200ms and 200 OK.

triage.question: Time of day pattern?
triage.answer: Noticed during demo load tests; not proven yet.

hypotheses.label: Application bug throwing 500 on some inputs
Upstream report service slow → gateway/client timeout
Browser-only race; Postman would be fine
Token intermittently rejected

actions.label: Send 10 sequential GETs in Postman with the same demo token
actions.feedback: Useful test — separates browser UI timing from API behavior.
actions.result: 7× 200 OK (~800ms–2s), 2× 500, 1× no response until Postman client timeout at 30s.
actions.evidence: Intermittent 500 and timeout confirmed outside the browser.

actions.label: Compare response bodies and headers for 500 vs timeout cases
actions.feedback: Useful test — status code is a clue, not the root cause.
actions.result: 500 responses include upstream_failed and X-Upstream-Latency: 18420. Timed-out calls show no body; gateway access log later shows 504 after 29s.
actions.evidence: 500 and timeout both point at slow/failing upstream — different symptoms, related dependency.

actions.label: Hit GET /api/demo/leads?limit=10 as a control
actions.feedback: Useful test — checks platform-wide outage vs endpoint-specific.
actions.result: Control endpoint consistently 200. Issue scoped to reports/summary.
actions.evidence: Other demo APIs healthy; failure localized to summary report dependency.

actions.label: Decode/refresh demo token and retry once
actions.feedback: Useful quick check — but 401 would be expected if auth were the issue.
actions.result: Token valid. Failures remain 500/timeout, never 401/403.
actions.evidence: Auth not implicated; failures are 500/timeout not unauthorized.

actions.label: Treat every failure as application 500 and stop investigating
actions.feedback: Premature — ignores timeouts and upstream latency headers.
actions.result: Incomplete story. Escalation would miss gateway 504 and X-Upstream-Latency evidence.
actions.evidence: Stopping at 500 alone loses the intermittent timeout / upstream clue.

actions.label: Document correlation IDs, ratios, and control-endpoint results for escalation
actions.feedback: Useful documentation — turns intermittent noise into a supportable ask.
actions.result: Note drafted: ~20% 500 upstream_failed, ~10% 504/timeout, control OK, corr demo-rpt-77f3. Ask: health of report-upstream dependency.
actions.evidence: Escalation includes frequencies, corr IDs, and distinction between 500 and timeout.

actions.label: Restart the demo API process without evidence
actions.feedback: Premature — restart is not root-cause analysis.
actions.result: Process bounce briefly clears symptoms; failures return under load. Root cause still unknown.
actions.evidence: Blind restart masked symptoms temporarily; did not identify upstream dependency.

completion.fixMessage: Intermittent upstream failure: same dependency surfaces as 500 (upstream_failed) or gateway/client timeout. Status codes are clues — escalate with corr IDs and control comparison.

scenarios.title: Hostname fails but IP works
scenarios.summary: Practice DNS vs connectivity: browser cannot resolve a demo hostname while a raw IP still loads the service.
scenarios.report: "https://demo-portal.example.test won't load — DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN. Colleague said try http://203.0.113.40 and that page loads. Is the server down?"
scenarios.objective: Show that the service can be up while name resolution fails, and capture nslookup evidence before blaming the application.
scenarios.impact: Users depending on the hostname cannot reach the demo portal; IP workaround works for technicians only.
scenarios.note: All hostnames and IPs are documentation/demo ranges (example.test / TEST-NET). Not a real outage claim.

triage.question: Exact browser error?
triage.answer: DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN for demo-portal.example.test

triage.question: Does IP access work?
triage.answer: http://203.0.113.40 serves the demo landing page.

triage.question: VPN or alternate DNS tried?
triage.answer: Not yet.

triage.question: Same failure on phone hotspot?
triage.answer: Unknown — good isolation question.

hypotheses.label: DNS record missing or wrong resolver
Application server is down
Firewall blocks hostname but not IP
Local hosts file override

actions.label: Open https://demo-portal.example.test in the browser
actions.feedback: Useful test — captures the user-facing failure mode.
actions.result: Chrome shows DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN. No HTTP response received.
actions.evidence: Hostname fails at DNS before any HTTP exchange.

actions.label: Open http://203.0.113.40 (demo IP)
actions.feedback: Useful test — separates name resolution from service availability.
actions.result: Demo landing page loads. Service is reachable by IP.
actions.evidence: Service up on 203.0.113.40 — not a total outage.

actions.label: Run nslookup demo-portal.example.test
actions.feedback: Useful test — simulated DNS evidence for escalation.
actions.result: nslookup returns NXDOMAIN from 192.0.2.53. No A/AAAA records.
actions.snippet:
> nslookup demo-portal.example.test
Server:  dns-demo.example.test
Address: 192.0.2.53

*** dns-demo.example.test can't find demo-portal.example.test: Non-existent domain
actions.evidence: nslookup NXDOMAIN — DNS record absent or not published to this resolver.

actions.label: Reverse-check: nslookup 203.0.113.40
actions.feedback: Useful optional context — PTR may be absent even when A should exist.
actions.result: No PTR found. Confirms IP is reachable but name mapping is incomplete in demo DNS.
actions.snippet:
> nslookup 203.0.113.40
*** Can't find server name for address 203.0.113.40: Non-existent domain
actions.evidence: No reverse mapping; forward lookup already failed with NXDOMAIN.

actions.label: Escalate as application outage without DNS evidence
actions.feedback: Premature — IP access already proves the service can respond.
actions.result: Escalation would misroute to app owners. DNS owners need the NXDOMAIN evidence instead.
actions.evidence: Skipping DNS checks risks wrong queue and delayed fix.

actions.label: Flush local DNS cache and retry hostname
actions.feedback: Useful hygiene step — here NXDOMAIN persists, so not just stale negative cache.
actions.result: After flush, hostname still NXDOMAIN. Resolver has no record to cache.
actions.evidence: Local flush did not restore resolution — publish/fix DNS record required.

actions.label: Inspect local hosts file for demo-portal.example.test
actions.feedback: Useful quick OS check.
actions.result: No entry for demo-portal.example.test. Hosts file not the cause.
actions.evidence: Hosts file clean — failure is resolver-side NXDOMAIN.

completion.fixMessage: Service reachable by IP; hostname returns NXDOMAIN. Escalate to DNS with nslookup output — not an application down incident.

scenarios.title: Turn a vague complaint into a structured bug report
scenarios.summary: Practice gathering expected vs actual, environment, and evidence, then generate a structured report from incomplete user language.
scenarios.report: "The export is broken. It doesn't work when I need it. Please fix ASAP."
scenarios.objective: Interview for missing fields and produce a ticket-ready report with expected/actual, steps, impact, and evidence.
scenarios.impact: Unclear — until scoped, severity and owner queue cannot be decided.
scenarios.note: Practice scenario with fictional export feature — not a production defect record.

triage.question: Which export?
triage.answer: Not specified in the original message.

triage.question: Expected vs actual?
triage.answer: Missing — only broken / doesn't work.

triage.question: When did it last work?
triage.answer: Unknown.

triage.question: Who is blocked?
triage.answer: Single reporter so far; scope unknown.

hypotheses.label: CSV export fails for leads list
PDF export fails on report page
Role cannot export (permission)
User error / wrong menu — not a defect

actions.label: Ask which screen and export type (CSV / PDF / XLS)
actions.feedback: Useful — unlocks the feature scope section of the report.
actions.result: Reporter: Leads list → Export CSV. Not PDF.
actions.evidence: Scope: Leads list CSV export.

actions.label: Capture expected vs actual in the reporter's words
actions.feedback: Useful — core of a structured bug report.
actions.result: Expected: CSV downloads. Actual: button spins 10s then toast Export failed (code EXP-204).
actions.evidence: Expected: CSV download. Actual: EXP-204 toast after spin.

actions.label: Gather environment: role, browser, tenant, time
actions.feedback: Useful — unlocks environment section.
actions.result: Counselor · Chrome 126 · demo-staging · 2026-08-11 14:22 IST · Lead filters: Status=Open.
actions.evidence: Environment recorded for reproduction.

actions.label: Write numbered reproduction steps with the reporter
actions.feedback: Useful — unlocks steps section.
actions.result: 1) Sign in as counselor 2) Open Leads 3) Filter Status=Open 4) Click Export CSV 5) Observe EXP-204.
actions.evidence: Five-step repro path agreed with reporter.

actions.label: Set Priority=Critical without impact details
actions.feedback: Premature — priority needs impact and urgency context.
actions.result: Ticket would overstate urgency. Only one counselor blocked on a non-billing export in demo.
actions.evidence: Critical without impact evidence is poor ticket hygiene.

actions.label: Attach toast screenshot and any network failure snippet
actions.feedback: Useful — unlocks evidence section.
actions.result: Screenshot of EXP-204 + Network: POST /api/demo/exports/leads → 500 {"code":"EXP-204"}.
actions.evidence: HTTP 500 EXP-204 export_worker_unavailable captured.

actions.label: Generate structured bug report from gathered fields
actions.feedback: Useful — assembles the ticket from unlocked sections.
actions.result: Structured report ready: summary, env, steps, expected/actual, evidence EXP-204, impact=one counselor blocked on CSV export, severity medium / priority normal pending SLA policy.
actions.snippet:
Summary: Leads CSV export fails with EXP-204
Expected: CSV downloads
Actual: Toast Export failed (EXP-204) after ~10s
Evidence: POST /api/demo/exports/leads → 500 export_worker_unavailable
Impact: Single counselor; workaround: copy table manually
actions.evidence: Complete structured report generated from gathered fields.

actions.label: File ticket with original text only: export is broken
actions.feedback: Low-information — shifts investigation cost to the next queue.
actions.result: Ticket rejected by triage bot for missing expected/actual and steps.
actions.evidence: Vague report fails intake quality checks.

completion.fixMessage: Structured report assembled: Leads CSV export → EXP-204 / export_worker_unavailable with env, steps, and expected vs actual.

scenarios.title: Choose what belongs in an escalation handover
scenarios.summary: Practice good vs weak escalation content: evidence and asks beat emotion and bare please fix messages.
scenarios.report: "Still broken. Escalating to L2. They need to fix this now. User is angry."
scenarios.objective: Build a handover that an L2 engineer can act on: context, evidence, impact, and a clear ask — without noise.
scenarios.impact: Demo counselor blocked on Lead #1842 updates; anger is real but not a substitute for evidence.
scenarios.note: Fictional ticket DEMO-338 for handover practice — not a real customer escalation.

triage.question: What was already tried at L1?
triage.answer: Reproduced 403 as counselor; admin succeeds; Edge same result.

triage.question: What is the ask for L2?
triage.answer: Not stated in the draft — only fix this now.

triage.question: SLA / urgency basis?
triage.answer: Single user blocked on non-billing workflow; severity medium pending policy.

triage.question: Attachments?
triage.answer: None yet on DEMO-338.

hypotheses.label: Evidence-rich handover enables L2 action
Emotion-only escalation will bounce
Wrong queue if framed as network outage

actions.label: Include reproduction steps and roles compared (counselor vs admin)
actions.feedback: Useful — good escalation content.
actions.result: Handover gains: counselor PATCH 403; admin PATCH 200 on Lead #1842; Edge+Chrome.
actions.evidence: Role comparison and repro steps added to DEMO-338.

actions.label: Attach HTTP snippet with reason role_lacks_permission
actions.feedback: Useful — concrete evidence for RBAC owners.
actions.result: Snippet attached. L2 can search permission matrix without re-discovering the 403.
actions.evidence: HTTP 403 payload attached to escalation.

actions.label: Write a clear ask: confirm counselor lead.write in role matrix
actions.feedback: Useful — escalations need an actionable ask.
actions.result: Ask field set. L2 knows the intended next check.
actions.evidence: Clear ask recorded on DEMO-338.

actions.label: Escalate with only: user is angry, fix immediately
actions.feedback: Low-information — emotion without evidence gets bounced.
actions.result: L2 returns ticket: Need repro, expected/actual, and logs.
actions.evidence: Emotion-only handover rejected.

actions.label: Route to Network because it feels like access issue
actions.feedback: Premature / misroute — evidence already shows authorization 403.
actions.result: Network queue declines: connectivity OK; 403 is application authz.
actions.evidence: Wrong queue wastes SLA clock.

actions.label: State impact and proposed severity/priority with rationale
actions.feedback: Useful — separates severity from loudness.
actions.result: Impact: one counselor blocked on lead updates. Severity: medium. Priority: normal unless SLA policy elevates single-user authz bugs.
actions.evidence: Impact and priority rationale included.

actions.label: Paste the user's password into the ticket for L2 convenience
actions.feedback: Premature and unsafe — never put credentials in tickets.
actions.result: Blocked by policy. Credentials removed; reminder logged.
actions.evidence: Credential sharing rejected — use demo IDs only.

completion.fixMessage: Good handover: repro, HTTP evidence, impact, and a clear RBAC ask. Emotion-only and wrong-queue paths bounce.

scenarios.title: Multi-role UAT matrix for a demo SaaS workflow
scenarios.summary: Run Admin / Counselor / Student checks on the same workflow and record pass/fail by role — not a single happy-path click.
scenarios.report: "UAT sign-off requested for Lead assign → note → status change. Please confirm all roles behave correctly before demo day."
scenarios.objective: Execute a minimal multi-role matrix, catch role gaps, and document results with evidence per cell.
scenarios.impact: Demo day risk if only admin happy-path was tested.
scenarios.note: Simulated UAT matrix inspired by multi-role SaaS thinking — not a client UAT sign-off record.

triage.question: Which roles are in scope?
triage.answer: Admin, Counselor, Student (demo personas).

triage.question: Critical workflow?
triage.answer: Assign lead → add note → change status.

triage.question: Prior testing?
triage.answer: Admin path only smoke-tested last week.

triage.question: Pass criteria?
triage.answer: Each role matches expected allow/deny; failures logged with HTTP status.

hypotheses.label: Admin full path passes
Counselor status change denied unexpectedly
Student can see or mutate leads they should not

actions.label: Admin: assign Lead #1842, add note, set status Contacted
actions.feedback: Useful — baseline allow path.
actions.result: PASS. All three steps succeed with 200 responses.
actions.evidence: Admin matrix row: assign/note/status = PASS.

actions.label: Counselor: open assigned lead, add note, change status
actions.feedback: Useful — primary persona path.
actions.result: Note POST 200. Status PATCH 403 role_lacks_permission. FAIL on status change.
actions.evidence: Counselor: note PASS, status FAIL (403).

actions.label: Student: attempt to open Lead #1842 detail
actions.feedback: Useful — deny-path check.
actions.result: GET returns 403. Student cannot open counselor lead. PASS (expected deny).
actions.evidence: Student lead detail correctly denied.

actions.label: Student: attempt PATCH status on Lead #1842
actions.feedback: Useful — confirms no write leak.
actions.result: PATCH 403. No status change. PASS (expected deny).
actions.evidence: Student write correctly denied.

actions.label: Sign off UAT after admin-only happy path
actions.feedback: Premature — misses counselor gap already present.
actions.result: Sign-off would be false confidence. Counselor status change still 403.
actions.evidence: Admin-only UAT is insufficient for multi-role SaaS.

actions.label: Record full pass/fail matrix with evidence links
actions.feedback: Useful documentation for demo-day go/no-go.
actions.result: Matrix logged: Admin PASS/PASS/PASS; Counselor note PASS / status FAIL; Student read/write DENY PASS. Blocker: counselor lead.write.
actions.snippet:
| Role | Assign | Note | Status |
| Admin | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| Counselor | n/a | PASS | FAIL 403 |
| Student | DENY | DENY | DENY |
actions.evidence: UAT matrix documented with blocker on counselor status update.

actions.label: Skip deny-path tests to save time
actions.feedback: Low-information — miss permission leaks.
actions.result: Student leak checks never run. Residual risk remains.
actions.evidence: Skipping deny paths weakens UAT confidence.

completion.fixMessage: Matrix complete: admin OK, student denies OK, counselor status change blocked (403). Do not sign off until lead.write is fixed and retested.

scenarios.title: Validate a simulated fix for counselor lead updates
scenarios.summary: A fix was applied in demo-staging — choose strong vs weak validation steps before calling it done.
scenarios.report: "Dev says counselor lead.write is fixed on demo-staging. Can you validate so we can close DEMO-338?"
scenarios.objective: Retest the failing path, a regression control, and a deny-path so the fix is confirmed — not assumed.
scenarios.impact: Closing without validation risks shipping a broken counselor workflow again.
scenarios.note: Simulated fix validation in a demo environment — not a production release claim.

triage.question: What changed?
triage.answer: Demo role matrix: counselor granted lead.write for assigned leads.

triage.question: Original failure?
triage.answer: PATCH Lead #1842 as counselor → 403 role_lacks_permission.

triage.question: Build / env marker?
triage.answer: demo-staging banner shows build 2026.08.11-fix1.

triage.question: Any known side effects?
triage.answer: Student role should remain denied.

hypotheses.label: Counselor can now update assigned leads
UI works but API still 403
Fix over-granted permissions to student

actions.label: Retest counselor PATCH status on assigned Lead #1842
actions.feedback: Useful — validates the original failing path.
actions.result: PATCH returns 200. Status Contacted. UI saves without toast error.
actions.evidence: Original failure path now PASS for counselor.

actions.label: Confirm both UI success and Network 200 (not UI-only)
actions.feedback: Useful — catches UI/API mismatch.
actions.result: UI checkmark and Network 200 align. No silent client-side fake success.
actions.evidence: UI and API both report success.

actions.label: Regression: admin can still update Lead #1842
actions.feedback: Useful control — ensure fix did not break admin.
actions.result: Admin PATCH still 200. No regression.
actions.evidence: Admin path remains PASS.

actions.label: Deny-path: student still cannot PATCH Lead #1842
actions.feedback: Useful — checks over-grant.
actions.result: Student PATCH still 403. Good — permissions not widened incorrectly.
actions.evidence: Student remains denied; no over-grant detected.

actions.label: Click around the home page once and close the ticket
actions.feedback: Low-information — does not retest the failing path.
actions.result: Home page loads. Zero evidence about lead.write fix.
actions.evidence: Weak validation — insufficient to close DEMO-338.

actions.label: Close ticket because developer said it is fixed
actions.feedback: Premature — validation is the support/UAT job.
actions.result: Policy: fixes need retest evidence before close.
actions.evidence: Trust-only closure blocked.

actions.label: Document validation results and close DEMO-338
actions.feedback: Useful once strong checks pass.
actions.result: Ticket closed with: counselor PASS, admin PASS, student DENY PASS, build 2026.08.11-fix1.
actions.evidence: Fix validated with matrix notes; DEMO-338 closed.

completion.fixMessage: Fix validated: counselor update works, admin unbroken, student still denied. Weak click-around / trust-only paths are insufficient.

scenarios.title: UI count disagrees with query result
scenarios.summary: Planned: practice reconciling a dashboard count with a demo SQL/API result without guessing production data.
scenarios.objective: Compare UI aggregate vs API/SQL filters and document the mismatch hypothesis.

scenarios.title: Demo service returns 503 on Linux host
scenarios.summary: Planned: practice service status, logs, and restart-vs-RCA thinking on a fictional Linux demo unit.
scenarios.objective: Check service state and logs before any restart; treat restart as last resort, not root cause.
